audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart on the page disagrees with the packet chart in three rows (1, 3 and 6) and the level 6 row credits neither side despite Hero's Entrance being the decisive global tool.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Galio, Swain, Swain]. Level 1 Swain out-ranges him with Death's Hand (750) against a 275-range Shield of Durand; level 3 his full kit and taunt even it; level 6 Hero's Entrance (180s at rank 1, 4000 range) makes him the map threat, which the page's own whys[4] already says.
audit.corrected: Rows flipped in matched pairs: win[0]/phases[0].side to Swain, win[2]/phases[2].side to Skill, win[4]/phases[4].side to Galio.

audit.why: Spike set is right: Nevermove at 2, Hero's Entrance at 6 as HIS spike, first-item Liandry's before his anti-heal completes, and a Morellonomicon-era 2-item phase. Passive soul fragments heal AND permanently raise max health, which the ahead/late text already reflects.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text reworded only to fix the root mechanic; spike timings unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanical errors repeated across early, whys and spikes: (a) Nevermove is described as rooting Justice Punch 'mid-dash' on the throw, (b) Colossal Smash is called a shield and Shield of Durand an 'MR shield'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Nevermove 'then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits' — the root is on the RETURN pass, so a Galio who sidesteps the throw is doing exactly what you want; the mirror audit reached the same conclusion. Colossal Smash is a periodic empowered auto dealing bonus magic damage in an area, no shield involved; Shield of Durand is a charged damage-reduction stance ending in a taunt (275 range, 18/17/16/15/14s).
audit.corrected: Throw E past his step-up so the return pass catches him as he punches, then pull. Trade windows keyed to Justice Punch's real cooldown of 11/10/9/8/7 seconds, not the stated 13.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'that 13-second window' for Justice Punch appears twice.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7s. By the mid-lane levels it is 9s, not 13.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells the player that Justice Punch cuts off retreat.
audit.why: Galio's E dashes through and knocks up, and Swain has no dash of his own — the escape problem is real and unstated.
audit.corrected: Covered inside the mid rewrite: hold Flash for his punch angle, not for damage.

edits.before: Both kits are online but he has no hard CC yet and your W cone poke bounces off his passive Colossal Smash shield — trade softly and bank E for level 2.
edits.after: Only Q is up and Colossal Smash is bonus magic damage on his auto, not a shield — Death's Hand out-ranges him, so win the chip war and bank E for level 2.

edits.before: Nevermove goes live and catches Justice Punch cleanly mid-dash: root him stepping forward, passive-pull the soul fragment, and W-slow to deny his escape.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the wave's return pass, not the throw: cast it past his step-up so it catches him as he punches, then pull him in and W-slow the escape.

edits.before: Full kit on both sides, but his W taunt and MR shield now eat your Q burst — trade only when his Justice Punch is on its 13-second cooldown.
edits.after: Full kit both sides, but Shield of Durand's reduction and taunt eat your Q burst — trade only while Justice Punch sits on its 9-second cooldown.

edits.before: His W magic-resist shield scales with his MR purchases and short trades favour him; fish for E roots on the Justice Punch cooldown and avoid extended all-ins without R.
edits.after: Shield of Durand cuts damage while charged and his MR buys stack on top, so short trades favour him; fish for E roots on Justice Punch's cooldown and avoid all-ins without R.

edits.before: Nevermove goes live — the matchup rule starts here: Galio's Justice Punch can be rooted mid-dash, so every time he steps up to E you have a free root into W-slow into Q-burst.
edits.after: Nevermove goes live — and it roots on the return pass, not the throw: cast it past his step-up so the wave catches him mid-punch, then pull and follow with W-slow into Q-burst.

edits.before: Level 1 is a Q-into-Q chip war. His Colossal Smash empowered auto and W magic-resist shield let Galio absorb your Death's Hand bolts without taking real damage, so do not blow mana blasting full Q cones into his shield. Walk up, collect a fragment off his passive auto, and hold E. The lane opens at level 2: Nevermove catches Justice Punch cleanly mid-dash — any time he steps up with that gap-closer available you can root him in place, drag the Soul Fragment out with the passive pull, then drop Vision of Empire on him while he is grounded. This two-level window before he gets his full taunt kit is the most reliable trade pattern you have.
edits.after: Level 1 is a Q-into-Q chip war. Colossal Smash is bonus magic damage on his auto, not a shield — what actually eats your Death's Hand bolts is Shield of Durand, so poke while that stance is down and never blast full cones into it. Walk up, collect a fragment, and hold E. The lane opens at level 2: Nevermove roots on the wave's return pass, so throw it past his step-up and it catches him as he punches, then pull him in and drop Vision of Empire while he is held. Justice Punch is down 11 seconds at rank 1, and that gap before his taunt comes online is your most reliable trade pattern.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely even. His W damage-reduction taunt eats your Q burst and his stacking MR begins to blunt the poke; your soul-stack count and max HP are climbing but you have not hit R sustain yet, so short trades actually favour him. Fish for E roots when Justice Punch is on cooldown — that 13-second window is when you trade, not when it is available. At 6 the calculus inverts in his favour globally: Hero's Entrance is a map-wide win button and he will shove into your tower and disappear. Do not chase him under tower. Shove back, drop a Vision of Empire ward on the river mouth, and either follow or take the plate gold. Your Demonic Ascension does win the pure 1v1 at this level if he stays, but he will not stay.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely even. Shield of Durand's damage reduction eats your Q burst and his MR buys blunt the poke; your soul stacks and max HP are climbing but you have no R sustain yet, so short trades favour him. Fish for E roots while Justice Punch is on cooldown — that 9-second window is when you trade, not when it is up. It also cuts your retreat, and you have no dash, so hold Flash for his punch angle rather than for damage. At 6 the map tilts to him: Hero's Entrance is a 180-second global and he will shove into your tower and vanish. Do not chase under tower. Shove back, drop Vision of Empire on the river mouth, and either follow or take the plate gold. Demonic Ascension wins the pure 1v1 if he stays, but he will not stay.

notes: Two errors were repeated in three places each: the Nevermove root is on the RETURN pass (Riot's own text), and Colossal Smash was described as a shield when it is an empowered auto — the shield/damage-reduction is Shield of Durand. Justice Punch's cooldown was stated as 13s twice; it is 11/10/9/8/7. Level chart on the page disagreed with the packet chart in three rows; proposed as matched full/content pairs in one group. Left 'late' untouched: it claims a flash-taunt can interrupt Demonic Ascension, which I cannot verify from the kits (R is a transform with no channel flag), so it is recorded as unverified rather than rewritten.
